That’s not how the system works. But your idea is closer to reality a bit
At time t=1 you place an order, all the bots place their orders and the matching happens
At time t=1.5 all orders are matched and cleared.

At time t=2 you send your new orders or old orders again.
All the bots place their orders and the matching happens.
At time t=2.5 all the orders are matched and cleared
The orders that are better will always be matched. But the order of incoming orders is not delayed. It is simultaneous

Imagine you built a system like this. In no details.

1. You build smaller systems that represent traders in the market, they may look like random walks per say.
2. You build an orderbook system, something like a simple database, holding orders sent by your traders.
3. You build a matching system, that finds the closest matching sell orders and buy orders in your orderbook system.
4. Depending on how serious you want to be you build something like a poisson process to propose events, like news impacting traders.

Now IMC has very clearly not simply put out random walker traders.
So ur saying it’s not random walk or it is?
I'm saying, you could surely try to squeeze the ocean into a tea cup. But you may loose complexity

I did a really bad version of a similar system many years ago, coming from the same thinking as everyone else here.

Build a class for traders.
Implement parameters like resistance, desired buy, sell prices, desired drift, desired inventory, basic strategy, and so on.
Those parameters on a trader class would than turn into something like a geometric brownian motion when matching with other traders. But that just fails to simulate the real market behaviours
So basically don’t overcomplicate it?

In essence, markets are far more complex than brownian motion or random walks. 
Don't expect your grad books to be able to tell you anything about them.
